faf4480c2e9fa0217e8eb9413078470a84ac0924.summary: The Register article (4 June 2012) reports on Tinba, a 20KB banking Trojan also known as Zusy. It hooks into browsers, uses Man in the Browser tricks to alter banking sites and get around two-factor authentication, and steals login data. Its command-and-control traffic is RC4-encrypted and goes to four hardcoded domains. Researchers at CSIS Security say antivirus detection of the analysed samples is low. The article compares Tinba with ZeuS and the Flame toolkit. Most of the page is unrelated news.

hedges: The report says it had nothing to substantiate a strictly technical connection between Moonlight Maze and Turla at the start of its work.
The authors say the provenance is likely, but one link is still missing, and more hard technical evidence is needed to confirm that Moonlight Maze is Turla.
The Turla link is a working hypothesis; the report says the earlier forensic evidence was destroyed and could not be tested directly.
The Storm Cloud link is stated as a belief and rests partly on a 2001 press report that the authors cite.
Penquin Turla dating is inferred from statically linked library and kernel versions, which the report says are not equivalent to PE compile timestamps.
The 2006 start date for Turla's Windows toolkits comes from unpublished third-party research that the report does not publish.
Visibility is limited: the log data covers October 1998 to March 1999 and only one UK staging server, and the report says other staging servers may be more numerous.

fa2349d8a5f0a8d211d60e45781ef4e01776981a.summary: Unit 42 (Palo Alto Networks) threat brief on Operation MidnightEclipse, the initial exploitation of CVE-2024-3400, a command injection flaw in PAN-OS GlobalProtect. Most attempts were unsuccessful; a few led to file copies or interactive command execution. The actor tried three times to install a Python backdoor called UPSTYLE, failed, and used a cron job backdoor that pulled commands from an external server instead. Fixes are in PAN-OS hotfix releases, and Threat Prevention IDs 95187, 95189 and 95191 block attacks. Volexity is credited with finding the issue.
